blocks.explanation:
Yahan do functions ka product hai: algebraic \(x^7\) aur logarithmic \(\ln x\).
Find karna hai is product ka integral.
Sawal yeh hai ke first function kaun bane? Agar \(x^7\) ko first banayein to \(\ln x\) ko integrate karna parega, jo mushkil hai.
ILATE mein L (logarithmic) A (algebraic) se pehle aata hai, is liye \(\ln x\) first aur \(x^7\) second.
Plan: ek dafa parts, phir ek aasaan power integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int x^7\ln x\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: integration by parts: \(f(x) = \ln x\) aur \(g(x) = x^7\), kyunke \(\ln x\) differentiate ho kar \(\frac{1}{x}\) ban jata hai aur \(x^7\) ka integral power rule se foran aata hai.

Doosre ka integral, pehle ka derivative
\[\int x^7\,dx = \dfrac{x^8}{8}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln x = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
Kyun: power rule \(\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\) se \(x^7\) ka integral \(\frac{x^8}{8}\). Yeh dono cheezein formula mein chahiye hongi, is liye pehle alag se likh li.

Parts ka formula lagayein
\[= \ln x\cdot\dfrac{x^8}{8} - \int \dfrac{x^8}{8}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8} - \dfrac{1}{8}\int x^7\,dx\]
Kyun: pehla \(\times\) doosre ka integral, minus \(\int\)(doosre ka integral \(\times\) pehle ka derivative). Andar \(\frac{x^8}{8}\cdot\frac{1}{x} = \frac{x^7}{8}\) bana, yani log ghayab ho gaya aur sirf power reh gayi.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{x^8}{x}\) ko \(x^7\) likhein, \(x^9\) nahi; divide karne par power ghat'ti hai.

Integrate karein
\[= \dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8} - \dfrac{1}{8}\cdot\dfrac{x^8}{8} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8} - \dfrac{x^8}{64} + c\]
Kyun: dobara power rule; \(\frac{1}{8}\cdot\frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{64}\).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8}\right) = x^7\ln x + \dfrac{x^7}{8}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^8}{64}\right) = \dfrac{x^7}{8}\]
Kyun: pehle term par product rule lagaya. Dono \(\frac{x^7}{8}\) minus ke saath cancel ho jate hain aur sirf \(x^7\ln x\) bachta hai, yani integrand.
